name: Solenne Neuralcrest Lattice Fascinator II
description:
A sculptural Spire-tier fascinator built around exposed neural-port hardware as the centerpiece of the design. The base is hand-formed iridescent bioresin — shifting from deep violet to pale gold depending on angle — mounted on a swept platinum wire frame that clips invisibly into the hair or scalp anchors. Radiating from the port hub, articulated filaments of gold-tone chromalloy wire extend in an asymmetric lattice, tipped with micro-droplets of cultured bioluminescent pearl.

The piece actively integrates with BCI hardware: the lattice filaments carry passive signal-routing capacity, functioning as a short-range social BCI relay while broadcasting the wearer's preferred public identity tag to nearby compatible devices. Couture-made. No two are identical.
functionality: Passive BCI social relay via chromalloy lattice: broadcasts identity tag, preferred contact protocols, and status tier to nearby BCI-enabled individuals. Scalp-anchor mounting is compatible with port-adjacent chrome hardware. Bioluminescent pearl elements glow faintly in low light without power draw.
what_it_says: Your neural hardware is not hidden — it is the jewel, and everyone in the room is already receiving your signal.
worn_by: elite social figures with visible BCI hardware
story_hooks: A Solenne Lattice II was found in a Tier 2 pawn shop — the identity tag still broadcast, and it belongs to someone officially listed as deceased.
The passive relay function has an undocumented secondary mode: it logs every BCI identifier within six meters, and Solenne's data arm has been quietly selling the records.
A Spire gala guest's fascinator began broadcasting a distress-coded identity tag mid-event — no one in the room admitted to noticing, but three people left early.
